title: Build Your First Robot: Pip
tagline: Build and drive a small wheeled robot, one step at a time.
description: Build a small wheeled robot step by step: parts, power, motors, sensors, line following and debugging.
outcome: After this course you can build a small wheeled robot that drives, avoids obstacles and follows a line.
whoFor: Learners who finished Course 1, or any beginner who wants to build a small wheeled robot.
prerequisites: Course 1 is helpful but not required.
outcomes: Identify the parts of a small robot kit
Make a robot drive and steer with two wheels
Use a distance sensor so the robot avoids walls
Find and fix problems step by step, and follow a line

finalActivity.title: Present your finished robot
finalActivity.prompt: Describe your finished robot: what it does, how you built it and one problem you fixed along the way. Say how you tested it on a track.

lessons.title: The Box of Parts
lessons.summary: Identify each part in a small robot kit and what it is for.

quiz.q: Which part in a robot kit is the brain?
quiz.why: The control board runs the program.

quiz.q: What do the motors do?
quiz.why: Motors spin the wheels so the robot moves.

quiz.q: What is a chassis?
options: The frame that holds all the parts
quiz.why: The chassis is the body everything is mounted on.

quiz.q: Why should you lay out and name every part before building?
options: So you know what each part is for and nothing is missing
quiz.why: Knowing the parts first prevents mistakes later.

lessons.title: Power
lessons.summary: Connect batteries safely and explain why polarity matters.

quiz.q: What does polarity mean for a battery?
options: Which end is positive and which is negative
quiz.why: Batteries have a plus and a minus side.

quiz.q: What can happen if you connect power the wrong way round?
quiz.why: Reversed power can burn or break electronic parts.

quiz.q: Before connecting the battery you should…
options: Check the plus and minus marks
quiz.why: Always check the marks before connecting.

quiz.q: If a wire or battery feels hot, you should…
quiz.why: Hot parts are a warning sign, so disconnect and check.

lessons.title: The Brain
lessons.summary: Power up the control board and see the first sign of life.

quiz.q: What is a good first sign that the control board is working?
options: A light turns on or blinks
quiz.why: A power or test light shows the board has power.

quiz.q: What does the control board do with a program?
quiz.why: The board follows the program's instructions in order.

quiz.q: If the board shows no light at all, check…
quiz.why: No light usually points to a power problem.

quiz.q: A simple first program is to…
quiz.why: Blinking a light proves the board and program work.

lessons.title: First Moves
lessons.summary: Fit the motors and wheels and explain how two wheels steer.

quiz.q: How can a robot with two driven wheels turn left?
options: Turn the right wheel faster than the left
quiz.why: Different wheel speeds make the robot turn.

quiz.q: If both wheels spin the same speed forward, the robot…
quiz.why: Equal speeds give a straight line.

quiz.q: If one wheel goes forward and the other backward, the robot…
quiz.why: Opposite directions make it spin on the spot.

quiz.q: Why should the wheels be fitted firmly?
options: So they do not wobble or slip off
quiz.why: Loose wheels cause unreliable movement.

lessons.title: First Eyes
lessons.summary: Make the robot drive and understand why it needs eyes.

quiz.q: Without sensors, a driving robot will…
options: Keep going even when it should stop
quiz.why: Without sensing, it cannot react to anything.

quiz.q: What does 'eyes' mean for a robot?
options: Sensors that tell it about the world
quiz.why: Sensors are the robot's eyes.

quiz.q: Why test driving on a clear floor first?
options: To see how it moves before adding complexity
quiz.why: Testing simple behaviour first makes problems easier to spot.

quiz.q: If the robot drives crooked, a likely cause is…
options: The two motors run at different speeds
quiz.why: Uneven motors make a robot veer.

lessons.title: Decisions
lessons.summary: Use a distance sensor so the robot decides what to do near a wall.

quiz.q: What does a distance sensor tell the robot?
quiz.why: It measures distance to objects.

quiz.q: A simple decision rule is…
options: If the wall is close, turn away
If the wall is close, speed up
quiz.why: Turning away avoids hitting the wall.

quiz.q: Why choose a distance at which to react?
options: To leave room to stop or turn in time
quiz.why: Reacting early gives space to stop.

quiz.q: This sense-then-decide pattern is called…
quiz.why: The robot senses, thinks, then acts.

lessons.title: When Things Go Wrong
lessons.summary: Find a problem step by step instead of guessing.

quiz.q: What is a good first step when a robot misbehaves?
options: Check one thing at a time, starting with power
quiz.why: Checking one thing at a time finds the real cause.

quiz.q: Why change only one thing between tests?
options: So you know which change fixed or broke it
quiz.why: One change at a time makes the cause clear.

quiz.q: A loose wire is best found by…
quiz.why: Checking connections one by one is simple and safe.

quiz.q: Writing down what you tried helps because…
options: You avoid repeating the same test
quiz.why: Notes stop you going round in circles.

lessons.title: Follow the Line
lessons.summary: Explain how a robot follows a line using light sensors.

quiz.q: How does a line sensor tell dark from light?
options: A dark line reflects less light than the floor
quiz.why: The sensor measures reflected light.

quiz.q: If the left sensor sees the line, the robot should…
options: Steer left to get back on it
quiz.why: Steer towards the side that sees the line.

quiz.q: Why do two sensors work better than one?
options: They show which side the line is on
quiz.why: Two sensors reveal the direction to correct.

quiz.q: A line-following robot works by repeating…
quiz.why: It runs the sense-think-act loop continuously.

lessons.title: Pip Meets the World
lessons.summary: Prepare a robot for light, floors and surprises outside the bench.

quiz.q: Why might strong sunlight confuse a line sensor?
options: It adds extra light the sensor did not expect
quiz.why: Bright light changes what the sensor reads.

quiz.q: Different floors can change a robot because…
options: Wheels grip differently on different surfaces
quiz.why: Grip changes how the robot moves.

quiz.q: Before taking a robot somewhere new, you should…
options: Test it there and adjust settings
quiz.why: Test in the real place and adjust.

quiz.q: A good way to handle surprises is to…
options: Plan a safe stop if something is wrong
quiz.why: A safe stop limits harm when something unexpected happens.

lessons.title: The Big Day
lessons.summary: Present a finished robot and explain what it can do.

quiz.q: When presenting your robot, start by saying…
quiz.why: Begin with the job so people understand the purpose.

quiz.q: Before a demo you should…
options: Run it a few times on the real track
Change the code at the last second
quiz.why: Practice runs catch problems early.

quiz.q: If the demo fails, a good response is to…
options: Explain what happened and try again
quiz.why: Calm debugging is part of robotics.

quiz.q: What shows that a robot is working well?
options: It does its job reliably several times
quiz.why: Repeatable success is the real test.
